title: People’s Mañanera August 24
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Higher Education 2026: More Options for Continuing Education  
** The Mexican government unveiled the Higher Education 2026 Platform, which
offers 37,503 available spaces for students. Young people will be able to
search for options by major and proximity to their homes, with no entrance
exams or fees.

**My Right, My Place: From Exclusion to the Right to Choose  
** Without the Comipems entrance exam, 74.2% of young people were admitted to
their first-choice program in upper secondary level education, compared to
26.2% in 2024. The model is already in place in 17 states. President Claudia
Sheinbaum emphasized that “this is known as inclusion—a stand against
exclusion and the ‘rejected’ as these students were once called.”

**Without the People’s Support, the Opposition Seeks Backing Abroad  
** Sheinbaum criticized PRI senator Alito Moreno for traveling to the United
States to speak out against Mexico and for hiring foreign consultants. She
said that the National Electoral Institute (INE) should review the legality of
those expenses and compared this behavior to 19th-century conservatism. “It’s
subservient; it’s treasonous,” she charged.

**In the Face of the Digital Smear Campaign: Stay Informed and Avoid Fake News  
** The President warned that public opinion trends and campaigns are
fabricated using money, AI, and bots. She recalled that Morena proposed
vetting candidates’ backgrounds and questioned the hypocrisy of the right-wing
forces, noting that former president Calderón had García Luna —who was
subsequently convicted of ties to drug trafficking— in his administration.

**In Response to Interference: The People and the Nation Come First  
** In response to attempts at interference in the country’s internal affairs,
the President called for upholding principles and defending Mexico’s dignity.
“The commitment to the people is always present; the commitment to the nation
is always present,” she explained.

**Cattle Exports Resume with Stricter Health Controls  
** Sonora has resumed cattle exports to the United States after strengthening
measures against the screwworm. It is important to take note of the new
sterile fly facility in Chiapas and the fact that, despite the shutdown, meat
production in Mexico has increased.
